source.title: Cat
source.quote: Adult domestic cats typically weigh 4–5 kg (8.8–11.0 lb).

mass_kg.note: Upper figure of the typical adult range; the source gives no mean.

source.title: Cat
source.quote: It averages about 46 cm (18 in) in head-to-body length and 23–25 cm (9.1–9.8 in) in height, with about 30 cm (12 in) long tails.

size_m.note: Average head-and-body length, tail not counted. Range is the standard +/-10%.

top_speed_mps.note: No published top speed found for this animal (the Cat article gives none, and Garland 1983's table has no domestic cat); category default (estimate 1 of 3, allowed by D-55).

source.title: Craniometric Characteristics of Selected Carnivora Species Kept in Captivity in Relation to Bite Force and Bending Strength of the Upper Canines (Różycka et al. 2024, Animals 14(9):1367)
source.quote: The bite force of smaller cats, such as domestic cats, is around 219–126 N on canines and 407–217 N on carnassials.

attack_force_n.note: Canine bite, estimated from skulls. Upper figure of the stated range; the source gives no mean (D-55).

attacks_per_s.note: No published strike rate found for this animal; category default (estimate 2 of 3, allowed by D-55).

endurance_s.note: No published fighting endurance found for this animal; category default (estimate 3 of 3, allowed by D-55).

aggression_0_1.note: aggression level 3: hunts or defends itself, avoids risky fights; cat fights are usually short.

group_tactics_0_1.note: group tactics level 1: solitary, always hunts alone.
